name: International Travel Checklist
description: An international travel checklist for going abroad, covering passport and visa, currency, health requirements, adapters, and embassy information.

items.text: Check your passport is valid and has enough blank pages
Confirm validity meets the destination's minimum
Renew your passport early if needed
items.note: Some countries require six months' validity beyond travel

items.text: Make copies of your passport, kept separately
Save digital copies in the cloud
Research visa requirements for your nationality
Apply for any visa or entry permit early
Check passenger forms or arrival declarations
Note any onward or return ticket rules
Verify rules with the destination's embassy
items.note: Visa and entry rules vary by country and change often

items.text: Check required and recommended vaccines early
Arrange travel insurance with overseas medical cover
Pack medicines with copies of prescriptions
Carry your vaccination and health records
Confirm health requirements via official sources
items.note: Health entry rules vary by country, so verify officially

items.text: Notify your bank of travel dates and countries
Arrange foreign currency or a travel card
Check card and ATM fees abroad
Set up an eSIM, local SIM, or roaming plan
Download offline maps and a translation app
Pack the right power adapters for the region
Add a voltage converter if devices need it
Bring a power bank for long travel days
Pack clothing suited to the climate and customs
Keep documents and electronics in your carry-on
Note the location of your country's embassy or consulate
Register with any traveler program your country offers
Save local emergency numbers
Share your itinerary with someone at home
Read official travel advisories for the destination
Confirm all entry rules before relying on this list
items.note: Passport, visa, and health rules vary by country and change without notice; verify with official government sources and the destination's embassy

faq.q: How is international travel different from domestic travel?
faq.a: International trips add passports, visas, foreign currency, different power plugs, and varied health and entry rules. A domestic travel checklist skips most of this. Use this list for going abroad and a domestic one for trips at home.

faq.q: How early should I prepare for international travel?
faq.a: Start two to three months ahead so there is time for passport renewals, visa applications, and any vaccines. Some countries require a passport valid for six months beyond your travel dates, so check early.

faq.q: How do I find out the entry requirements for a country?
faq.a: Entry and visa rules vary by country and change often. Check your own government's travel advice and the destination country's embassy or official immigration site rather than relying on unofficial sources.

faq.q: Do I need different power adapters abroad?
faq.a: Often yes. Plug types and voltage vary by region, so check your destination and pack the right adapter, plus a voltage converter if your devices need one. A universal adapter covers most trips.

faq.q: Is this international travel checklist printable?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF, start well ahead of departure, and verify visa, entry, and health requirements with official government sources and the destination's embassy.
